notesStmt.note: This draft was likely composed in late 1890 or early 1891.

This manuscript is a draft of a portion of the essay "American National Literature," which first appeared in the March 1891 issue of North American Review under the title, "Have We a National Literature?" before appearing in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) and Complete Prose Works (1892).

body.p: Perhaps, my friends, it is not only alone the free schools and newspapers—not only railroads, fa steam, or electricity—nort our all the iron, whea cotton, pork, and petroleum ‸or even the gold and silver and and a surplus of a hundred millions & more of our States—nor even the 14th and 15th Amendments—‸and a population of fifty sixty five millions and cash incalculable that can put These States highest or among the highest on the univers kosmical scale of History,—but perfect, cute and homely, moral Personalities—or great native literatures, and Arts, Sociologies something else is indispensable.
